name: Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport
before:
Canada's sixth busiest airport, 15 km south of downtown Ottawa, serving both Ottawa and Gatineau. It handled 4,866,236 passengers in 2025 and is a major hub for Porter Airlines, a focus city for Air Canada and Air Transat and the home base for Canadian North.

The detail worth knowing for a client flying onward to the United States: this is one of only nine Canadian airports with US border preclearance, so passengers clear American immigration here.

The terminal opened in October 2003, designed by Richard Brisbin and finished ahead of schedule. It was paid for in an unusual way, by putting up the airport parking rates from January 1997 and setting the money aside.

The site was a military base, CFB Uplands, and the Royal Canadian Air Force still keeps 412 Transport Squadron here, which flies Canadian and visiting government officials.

The airport is named after Sir John A. Macdonald and Sir George-Étienne Cartier.
after:
Canada's sixth busiest airport, 15 km south of downtown Ottawa. It handled more than 4.7 million passengers in 2025 and is a major hub for Porter Airlines and the home base for Canadian North. Air Canada and Air Transat also fly from here.

For a client flying on to the United States, one detail matters: the airport has US border preclearance, so passengers clear American border checks here.

The terminal opened in October 2003 and was finished ahead of schedule.

Once known as Uplands, the site was a military base. The airport's name honours two of Canada's Fathers of Confederation, Sir John A. Macdonald and Sir George-Étienne Cartier.

claims.note: No archived Wikipedia copy exists for YOW; source 1 is the article as it read today (revision of 23 September 2026, 18:43 UTC). Statistics Canada's 2025 table (released 21 July 2026) puts Ottawa sixth: Toronto Pearson, Vancouver, Montreal-Trudeau, Calgary, Edmonton, then Ottawa at 4,732,563, ahead of Winnipeg at 4,274,502. The one suppressed airport of any size, Toronto Billy Bishop, had 2.0 million in 2023, far below.

claims.claim: CFB Uplands; RCAF 412 Transport Squadron still here, flying government officials
claims.wasBefore: The site was a military base, CFB Uplands, and the Royal Canadian Air Force still keeps 412 Transport Squadron here, which flies Canadian and visiting government officials.
claims.why: The military base is kept (as Uplands). The RCAF's own page (modified 11 October 2022) says 412 Transport Squadron is based in the National Capital Region and is known for VIP transport, but does not say it is at the airport, and the operator mentions the squadron only in the 1950s. So 'still keeps it here' rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: non-stop flights to London (Air Canada to Heathrow, Air Transat to Gatwick)
claims.why: Held back: the old text never mentioned London, and it matters to UK agents. Air Canada flies Ottawa to London Heathrow (CTV, 23 September 2025: through the winter; Wikipedia: year round) and Air Transat began Ottawa to London Gatwick on 15 May 2026 for the summer (PAX, 8 October 2025; Wikipedia). The operator's destination map gives no text, so no source from the last 12 months confirms the Heathrow flights are still running; worth Andy adding once checked.
